    • Find gaps in a foundation shade range

shaderange

The shaderange package helps beauty product strategy managers decide where their next foundation launch could make the biggest difference. It compares the deep, medium and light shades a brand offers at Sephora and Ulta with the whole market, showing where the brand’s range is thinner than its competitors’ and where the market as a whole is thin. For each gap, it points to the competitor products that currently lead, giving a benchmark to catch up to or a chance to stand out.

The package contains:

  • foundation_shades: 6,774 foundation shades from 107 brands, collected from the Sephora and Ulta websites in early 2021
  • shade_supply(): summarises shade supply by lightness band
  • brand_gaps(): compares a brand’s shade mix with the market
  • run_app(): launches an interactive Shiny app for exploring brand gaps

Documentation website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-miriam0085/

Installation

Install the package from GitHub with:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-miriam0085")

Launch the app 

library(shaderange)
run_app()

Choose your brand and retailer in the sidebar. The app shows where your brand’s shade mix is thinner than the market and which competitor products lead those bands.

Example

Compare a brand’s shade mix with the market:

library(shaderange)
brand_gaps(foundation_shades, brand = "L'Oréal")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   band   brand_shades brand_share market_share     gap
#>   <fct>         <int>       <dbl>        <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 Deep             29       0.190        0.160  0.0297
#> 2 Medium           72       0.471        0.457  0.0138
#> 3 Light            52       0.340        0.383 -0.0435

A negative gap marks a band where the brand offers proportionally fewer shades than the market.

Data

The shade data come from The Pudding’s article The Naked Truth (2021), released under the MIT licence and accessed via TidyTuesday. The script data-raw/foundation_shades.R downloads the raw data from TidyTuesday, removes duplicate shades and saves the cleaned result as foundation_shades.
